summary.tagline: Lough Ree (Irish: Loch Rí), translated to English as King's Lake or King Lake,is a lake in the midlands of Ire

days.title: Northern Isles and Shorelines
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM start, after checking official access hours

stops.name: Lanesborough
stops.detail: At the northern end of the lake lies the small town of Lanesborough.

stops.name: Inchcleraun
stops.detail: In the northern part of Lough Ree lies the island of Inchcleraun (Irish Inis Cloithrinn), on which the remains of an early Christian monastery and churches are located.

stops.name: Saints Island
stops.detail: Saints Island is located west of Ballymahon in the eastern arm of Lough Ree in County Longford.

days.driving: Allow time between these sights; local travel times are not verified and conditions vary.

days.title: Southern Ports and Geological Formations
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM start, after checking official access hours

stops.name: Athlone
stops.detail: Lough Ree is accessible from Athlone at the southern end of the lake, where there is a harbor leading to the lake.

stops.name: Rindoon
stops.detail: Approximately in the middle of the western side of Lough Ree, at its narrow point between the northern and southern lake, lies Rindoon, a peninsula steeped in history.

stops.name: mushroom stones
stops.detail: In the vicinity of the lake, many so-called mushroom stones are found; these are mushroom-shaped limestone formations created by water erosion.
